result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.cmty_louvain()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Detect communities using Louvain multi-level optimization algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11211-L11352){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.cmty_louvain(resolution=1.0, attr_name=None, return_dict=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The Louvain method is a hierarchical algorithm that maximizes modularity through iterative optimization. It's the most widely-used community detection algorithm in practice due to its speed (`O(n log n)`) and quality on large networks. The method produces a dendrogram hierarchy but returns the partition with maximum modularity. Works only with undirected graphs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [resolution]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Resolution parameter controlling community size. Higher values favor smaller communities. Standard modularity uses resolution=1.0. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store community assignments in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `cmty_louvain`. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to community IDs (0-indexed, contiguous). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [RuntimeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on a directed graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Algorithm steps: 1. phase 1 (Local optimization): each node tries joining neighboring communities to maximize modularity gain `ΔQ` 2. phase 2 (Aggregation): communities are coarsened into super-nodes, creating a new network where each community becomes a single node 3. repeat until modularity converges (no further improvement) The resolution parameter tunes community size: - `resolution < 1.0`: Larger communities - `resolution = 1.0`: Standard modularity optimization - `resolution > 1.0`: Smaller communities The algorithm is deterministic but may produce different (equivalent) partitions depending on node ordering. Handles disconnected components naturally. Self-loops and multi-edges are currently not supported. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Detect communities in bridged triangles: ```python graph = ( Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_node(label="E") .add_node(label="F") ) # Build two complete triangles connected by bridge for i, j in [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]: graph.add_edge(i, j) graph.add_edge("C", "D") # Bridge for i, j in [("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]: graph.add_edge(i, j) communities = graph.cmty_louvain(return_dict=True) # Nodes in same triangle have same community ID node_a = graph.get_id_from_label("A") node_b = graph.get_id_from_label("B") node_c = graph.get_id_from_label("C") node_d = graph.get_id_from_label("D") assert communities[node_a] == communities[node_b] == communities[node_c] assert communities[node_d] == communities[graph.get_id_from_label("E")] # Control community granularity with resolution fine = graph.cmty_louvain(resolution=1.5, return_dict=True) # Smaller communities coarse = graph.cmty_louvain(resolution=0.5, return_dict=True) # Larger communities ``` Store as node attributes and chain: ::: {#8a58f2fb .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_node(label="E") .add_node(label="F") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="A") .add_edge(source="C", target="D") .add_edge(source="D", target="E") .add_edge(source="E", target="F") .add_edge(source="F", target="D") ) ( graph .cmty_louvain(attr_name="community") .colorize_node_attrs(node_attr_from="community", palette="viridis") .describe() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Number of nodes : 6 Number of edges : 7 Directed : False Density : 0.47 Average degree (min, max) : 2.33 (2, 3) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : False Bipartite : False Computations on nodes: - cmty_louvain() -> attr: 'community' (6 of 6 nodes) Node aesthetics: - color <- community via colorize (palette: "viridis") (values: #440154, #482777, 6 of 6 nodes) ``` ::: :::
